basis: Two deliverables of AFC-211, plus the check that keeps them wired together. (1) services/directus/compose.yml, transcribed from the outline in docs/planning/infra-spec.md section 4, which the issue names as a specification rather than a design question; the only addition to the outline is the `deploy-region` guard service. (2) services/directus/bin/assert-deploy-region.sh, the boot-time assertion that DEPLOY_REGION is present and well-formed as <ISO-3166-1 alpha-2>:<provider location code>, exiting 78 with a message naming the variable and where to set it. It runs as the guard service's entrypoint and every other service declares depends_on: deploy-region with condition service_completed_successfully, so `docker compose up` cannot start the stack without it passing. It is deliberately not in apps/web: DEPLOY_REGION is legitimately unset in dev and CI, and an assertion in the Nuxt boot path would fail both.
notCompliancePath: None of these four paths is guarded. scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh guards scripts/, services/directus/schema/ and tests/; compose.yml sits in services/directus/ and the two new files in services/directus/bin/, none of which is under a guarded prefix. R2 is narrower still (services/directus/schema/engine/**, services/directus/schema/migrations/**, tests/db/**, scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh) and names none of these. The issue anticipated this and directed that compose.yml stay in services/directus/ rather than services/directus/schema/; it has not been relocated. Verified by running the guard, which reports these paths as clean.
noValueCommitted: DEPLOY_REGION has no value in any committed file and none was set to make a check pass. services/directus/.env.example ships it empty, as AFC-171 rev 3 declared it; compose.yml references ${DEPLOY_REGION} and nothing else. Every value exercised by the two checks is a fixture with the synthetic country code QQ, which is not an assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, so no file in this change names a region. The `.env.example` placeholder shape XX:yyyy is itself a reject case in both the self-test and the wiring check, because a validator that accepted the documented example would let the example become the value by copy-paste.
verification: assert-deploy-region.sh --self-test: 23 cases, green, one per branch. check-deploy-region-wiring.mjs: 8 checks, green, covering compose wiring and end-to-end behaviour through the resolved entrypoint. Both were shown to be falsifiable rather than merely passing -- three mutants of the assertion (always-exit-0, placeholder accepted, location charset loosened) and four mutants of compose.yml (directus ungated, entrypoint stops asserting, a region value committed, guard set to restart) were each caught with a named failure, and the unmutated control stayed green. No Docker daemon is available in this workspace (dockerd cannot write /var/lib/docker or /run/docker), so `docker compose up` was not executed; the behaviour checks invoke the guard's resolved entrypoint and environment directly, and the wiring checks read the output of `docker-compose config --format json`. What that does NOT prove: that a real container actually blocks on the depends_on condition. That needs a daemon and is named as the remaining step.
doesNotClaim: A claim asserts authorship, not correctness. It is not a licence, it reviews nothing, and it cannot exempt any file from the retention-literal gate.
notDone: DEPLOY_REGION is unset and must stay unset until a human with authority to spend chooses a region at the moment a production VPS is bought (AFC-171 section 6 step 3). No server was bought, requested or configured; the board rejected both procurement approvals on 2026-10-06. The wiring check is not wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml -- it needs a Docker daemon, which ubuntu-latest has and this workspace does not, and adding it was not in this issue's scope.
